results.content: Our offices were just up the street from Grand Central, and only David DesRosiers, then MI’s vice president (now publisher of RealClearPolitics), and a couple of other colleagues, heading out, were still there. DesRosiers had a television on. “They’re dropping planes on us,” he said grimly. We watched the footage of the towers burning. The coverage was nervous and uncertain: How many planes were still in the air and unaccounted for? Then came reports that the Pentagon had been hit as well, and [...] Then the first tower collapsed.
